findings.description: SlowTraceHash(C::CrvHyp[FldRat]) calls TracesOfFrobenius(C,2^13:B0:=2^12), but no such signature exists: stock Magma (V2.29-8 installed here) defines TracesOfFrobenius only for (E::CrvEll[FldRat], B::RngIntElt) with no B0 parameter, and grep shows this package defines no TracesOfFrobenius intrinsic either (the name appears only in gl2points.m as a call on elliptic curves). Consequently EVERY call to SlowTraceHash raises 'Bad argument types', and with it: TraceHash(C::CrvHyp) for any genus != 2 curve (line 160 falls through to SlowTraceHash) and TraceHash(C::CrvHyp,E::CrvEll) for genus 3 (line 189) always fail. The code apparently assumes an unshipped intrinsic from Sutherland's smalljac Magma interface. Correct behavior: return TraceHash of a_p(C) = trace of Frobenius on H^1 = p+1-#C(F_p) at good window primes (with an Euler-factor computation at bad window primes). I validated that formula end-to-end against LMFDB: for the genus 2 curves 249.a.249.1 (y^2+(x^3+1)y=x^2+x) and 277.a.277.1, TraceHash(func<p|p+1-#ChangeRing(C,GF(p))>) equals the LMFDB Lhash (= trace hash) 1229180703233001291 and 639653774064676620, computed in ~0.5s.

TraceHash(C::CrvPln[FldRat]) calls TracesOfFrobenius(C,2^13:B0:=2^12); no TracesOfFrobenius signature for CrvPln exists in stock Magma V2.29-8 or in this package (see the SlowTraceHash finding), so the intrinsic fails on every input, including perfectly smooth plane quartics that pass the require. As a consequence TraceHash(C::CrvPln,E::CrvEll) (line 183) also always fails, since it calls TraceHash(C). Correct behavior: hash of a_p(C) = p+1-#C(F_p) at good window primes (the standard trace of Frobenius on H^1 of a smooth projective curve), with bad-prime Euler factors where needed; #RationalPoints(ChangeRing(C,GF(p))) works for CrvPln over finite fields (note plain # does not).

Three mutually inconsistent return conventions: the docstring says 'returns trace hash, zratio, moments' (h,z,m), the declared return types are 'SeqEnum,FldRatElt,RngIntElt' (suggesting m,z,h, and mistyping z which is a FldReElt, not FldRatElt), but the code (line 214) executes 'return z,m,h;' i.e. (zratio::FldReElt, moments::SeqEnum[FldReElt], hash::RngIntElt). A caller following the docstring will take the zero-trace ratio (a real number < 1) as the trace hash with no error raised. Correct behavior: docstring and declared types should match the actual return order (fixing the doc is the non-breaking choice; there are no callers inside this repo).
findings.proposed_fix:
Current lines 207-208:
intrinsic TraceStats(aplist::SeqEnum, w::RngIntElt:Moments:=6) -> SeqEnum,FldRatElt,RngIntElt
{ Given a list of ap values indexed by primes up to at least 2^13 and motivic weight w, returns trace hash, zratio, moments. }
Replacement:
intrinsic TraceStats(aplist::SeqEnum, w::RngIntElt:Moments:=6) -> FldReElt,SeqEnum,RngIntElt
{ Given a list of ap values indexed by primes up to at least 2^13 and motivic weight w, returns zratio, moments, trace hash. }
(Alternative, if the documented order is what downstream users expect: change line 214 to 'return h,z,m;' and declare '-> RngIntElt,FldReElt,SeqEnum' — but fixing the doc is non-breaking.)

findings.description: The docstring claims the returned value is sum_(2^12<p<2^13) |a_p(E)|*c_p, but the implementation replaces E by MinimalQuadraticTwist(jInvariant(E)) and zeroes a_p at bad primes of THAT curve, so the returned value generally differs from the documented formula: (a) when a window prime divides the conductor of E but not of the minimal twist, and (b) — more strikingly — for j=0/1728, where MinimalQuadraticTwist(j) minimizes over sextic/quartic twists, so curves that are NOT quadratic twists of each other (whose |a_p| genuinely differ) all receive the identical hash of the one minimal curve. The behavior (full twist-class invariance keyed by j) is very likely intentional; the docstring should say what is computed, like the UserProgram variant's docstring does.
findings.evidence:
Magma transcript:
> E1 := EllipticCurve([0,0,0,0,2]); E2 := EllipticCurve([0,0,0,0,3]);  // j=0, conductors 1728 and 3888
> IsQuadraticTwist(E1,E2);
false
> TwistHash(E1); TwistHash(E2);
275899985976071014
275899985976071014   // identical: both are the hash of MinimalQuadraticTwist(0) = [0,0,1,0,0] (27a3)
> TraceHash(func<p|Abs(TraceOfFrobenius(E2,p))>);  // the literal docstring value for E2 (all window primes are good for E2)
1003525965811339362   // differs from TwistHash(E2)
Also: E3 := QuadraticTwist(EllipticCurve("11a1"),4099); TwistHash(E3) eq TwistHash(EllipticCurve("11a1")) is true, while the literal hash of |a_p(E3)| differs (4099 is a window prime dividing N(E3)).

findings.description: Docstring typo, twice: line 181 and line 187 both say 'an elliptic curve E/q' where 'E/Q' is meant. Pure text fix; no behavioral impact.
findings.evidence: Line 181: '{ Given a smooth plane quartic curve C/Q and an elliptic curve E/q computes the hash ... }'. Line 187: '{ Given a hyperelliptic curve C/Q of genus 3 and an elliptic curve E/q computes the hash ... }'. Every other docstring in the file writes E/Q, C/Q.
findings.proposed_fix: In lines 181 and 187 replace 'an elliptic curve E/q' with 'an elliptic curve E/Q'.

findings.description: The genus 2 fast paths of TraceHash(C::CrvHyp) (line 162) and TwistHash(C::CrvHyp) (line 170) shell out to an external binary 'hashcurves' via Pipe with no availability check and no documentation of the dependency beyond an oblique header comment. When the binary is absent the user gets an opaque 'Runtime error in Pipe: Subprocess failed with exit status 127' rather than a meaningful message. On this machine the binary is not installed, so the genus 2 branch (lines 162-163, 170-171), including the c[#PrimesUpTo(p)-564] exceptional-prime correction and the euler() helper dispatch, could only be desk-checked, not executed. Desk-check details: the index map p=p_k -> c[k-564] is correct for the window p_565..p_1028 (verified #PrimesUpTo(4099)=565), and the aplist/c convention itself was validated against LMFDB g2c Lhash values by computing a_p independently. Suggest adding a require/System check with a clear error, and mentioning the hashcurves dependency in README.md.
findings.evidence:
Transcript: > TraceHash(HyperellipticCurve(x^5+x^2+x, x^2+x+1));
sh: 1: hashcurves: not found
Runtime error in 'Pipe': Subprocess failed with exit status 127
Reasoning for the desk-check: c[#PrimesUpTo(p)-564] maps p=4099 (the 565th prime) to c[1] and p=8191 (the 1028th prime) to c[464], matching the P[i] <-> c[i] pairing used by TraceHash(ap::UserProgram); the overall convention is pinned down by the LMFDB cross-checks (11.a, 249.a.249.1, 277.a.277.1).

coverage_notes: Executed and property-tested against independent oracles: TraceHash(ap::UserProgram), TraceHash(aplist::SeqEnum), TraceHash(E::CrvEll[FldRat]) (five curves vs LMFDB ec_classdata.trace_hash, including conductor 5077 inside the prime window, isogeny invariance via IsogenousCurves, distinctness across classes), TraceHash(E1,E2), TwistHash(ap::UserProgram), TwistHash(aplist), TwistHash(E::CrvEll) (quadratic-twist invariance incl. twisting by a window prime; j=0 sextic-twist behavior probed for the doc finding), TwistHash(E1,E2) (simultaneous-twist invariance), TraceHash(E::CrvEll[FldNum]) (restriction-of-scalars identity over Q(sqrt5), all 464 Euler factors), TraceHash(f::RngSerPowElt) (sparse integer series = 37a1, plus via eigenform), TraceHash(M::ModSym) (23.2.a.a with quadratic Hecke field vs LMFDB mf_newforms.trace_hash — exercises the double-Trace path; 11.2.a.a also verified during probing), TraceStats (w=0,1,2; hash/zratio/moments checked against inline brute force and the Sato-Tate second moment; return-order doc-bug found; the odd-w concern about rational exponents is a non-issue — Magma V2.29-8 returns FldReElt for n^(1/2)). Executed and found broken (findings, excluded from tests): SlowTraceHash(CrvHyp), TraceHash(CrvPln), TraceHash(CrvHyp genus!=2), TraceHash(CrvHyp,E), TraceHash(CrvPln,E) — all fail on the nonexistent TracesOfFrobenius(CrvHyp/CrvPln,...:B0) signature; the aplist convention they should implement was independently validated against LMFDB g2c Lhash (249.a.249.1, 277.a.277.1) via direct point counts, which the test fragment covers. Read/desk-checked only (cannot execute — external 'hashcurves' binary not installed): the genus 2 fast paths of TraceHash(CrvHyp) and TwistHash(CrvHyp) (lines 158-172) including the euler() helper and the c[#PrimesUpTo(p)-564] exceptional-prime index arithmetic (verified correct on paper; noted the >300s-per-25-primes slowness of Magma's EulerFactor(CrvHyp,p) fallback that the header comment warns about). The hardcoded 464-entry constant table c (lines 7-99) is pinned down transitively by the LMFDB hash matches rather than verified value-by-value against the paper.
